$comment: Synthetic retail data contract for GitHub Issue #2.
THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF EVERY EXPECTED VALUE. It is read by the
generator notebook (to produce the data) and independently by the
validation notebook and tests/issue2-validation.tests.ps1 (to assert the
result). Expected values are therefore declared BEFORE the run, in the
repository, and are never derived from the run under test.
docs/review-evidence-standard.md: 'Expected values come from the ticket,
never derived from the run under test - self-derived expectations make
The generation is pure integer arithmetic with no random number generator,
so the same contract always produces byte-identical source data. That is
what makes the second-run idempotency assertion meaningful.
Contains no real Fabric, tenant or user identifier. Safe for a public repo.

$comment_defects: Each defect row is built from a clean template and mutates EXACTLY ONE
field, so the reject categories are mutually exclusive and the expected
quarantine breakdown below is exact rather than approximate.
Duplicate rows are byte-copies of valid lines: they pass every quality
rule and must be removed by deduplication, not by quarantine. That is
deliberate - it separates 'rejected because bad' from 'removed because
repeated', which are different failures with different fixes.

expected.$comment: Every number below is arithmetic from 'generation' above and is asserted at runtime.
$comment_quarantineByReason: orphan_product and invalid_discount are expected to be 0. They are listed
explicitly rather than omitted: 0 asserts that the rule ran and matched
nothing, whereas omission would leave a rule that never executes
indistinguishable from one that executed cleanly.
$comment_rowConservation: 5170 = 5040 + 70 + 60. Every source row is accounted for exactly once;
no row is silently dropped. This identity is computed from three
independently written tables, so it cannot be satisfied by a bug that
affects them all in the same direction.
